text:
viv: Heads-up: installed redwoodctl via snap on Ubuntu 22.04 and hit a weird config/auth mismatch when running local-serve inside a docker-in-docker dev container.

ash: oh snap package? what happened exactly?

viv: snap confines the binary. `redwoodctl config list` showed profiles in `/root/snap/redwoodctl/common/.redwood` but my project (running in docker) expects `~/.redwood` in the host home. local-serve couldn't find the token and tried to spawn `redwoodctl login` but that run couldn't access the host browser and just hung.

yun: yeah snap mounts can make home dir access funky. also snaps auto-update which sometimes replaces the binary path under `/snap/bin` and breaks PID-based locks.

viv: the annoying part: no clear error. local-serve just showed "no token found" and then a blank spinner. took us a while.

ash: workarounds?

viv: for my team we ended up doing this: 1) don't use snap for dev machines; use the distro repo/package or the install script. 2) if you must use snap, set REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR to a path outside snap's confinement (e.g., `$HOME/.redwood`), make sure snap has home access: `sudo snap connect redwoodctl:home` and restart your shell.

yun: +1. Another trick is to create a small shim script in your PATH that calls `/snap/bin/redwoodctl --config-dir $HOME/.redwood "$@"` so spawned processes inherit the same config dir.

viv: example shim I put in ~/bin/redwoodctl:

```
#!/bin/bash
export REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.redwood"
exec /snap/bin/redwoodctl "$@"
```

and `chmod +x ~/bin/redwoodctl` and ensure ~/bin is before /snap/bin in PATH.

ash: nice. also consider adding `--no-open` and `--device` in spawn calls so it doesn't try to open a browser from a sandboxed snap. local-serve should pass those flags when it detects noninteractive env.

snap-bot: FYI snaps require the home plug for access to $HOME. Connect: `sudo snap connect redwoodctl:home`. See https://snapcraft.io/docs/interfaces

yun: another gotcha: launching docker from within a snap can drop environment variables. we saw REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR missing in the child container. local-serve should explicitly pass `--config-dir` when it spawns redwoodctl, or better inherit the env via `env -i` style avoidance.

viv: filed a tiny issue: PDE-621 local-serve should preserve REDWOODCTL_CONFIG_DIR and prefer `--no-open` for non-tty.

devex-bot: Feature request logged: PDE-621 preserve config dir when spawning CLI; add non-open device fallback and clearer error when confined binary cannot access host resources.

ash: for CI we added a preflight check: `redwoodctl --version || (echo "redwoodctl not available or confined; try non-snap install" && exit 1)` so jobs fail early with a hint.

yun: and for reproducible local dev, team decided to avoid snap and use the tarball install into /opt/redwoodctl with a systemd user unit for local-serve. helps with consistent env across shells.

viv: PR with docs + shim snippet: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2701 (draft). once merged i'll update the quickstart.

ash: sweet. small ask: when spawn fails due to confinement, local-serve should log the underlying errno (EACCES/ENOENT) and include a one-line remediation (e.g., 'snap confinement: run "sudo snap connect redwoodctl:home" or use non-snap install'). saved us hours.

devex-bot: Note added to PDE-621: include errno-based messages for spawn failures.

viv: thanks all. moving project to non-snap install for now. will follow up when docs PR merges. :shipit:
